messages:
Sam Klein: Heads-up — ran the dedicated-pool autoscale soak overnight and saw a ~15% P50 regression versus last week's baseline. Data in the perf dashboard: https://redwood.internal/perf/runs/1759 :thinking_face:
perf-bot: automated-run: dedicated-pool-autoscale-2026-03-16 completed. Summary: P50 +15%, P95 +8%, tail CPU/PCIe stalls observed. Full logs -> /artifacts/1759/logs.tar.gz
Dmitri Chen: interesting. Any changes to kernel selection or quantization kernels deployed in that window? I pushed a kernel selection tweak last Friday (commit 9c3b7f) to prefer fused-attn for short context.
Elaine Park: tagging the rollout: 9c3b7f landed to canary at 2026-03-13 02:11 UTC. We did enable continuous-batching heuristic change in same canary: batch_policy.v2 (prefer latency-aware batching).
Maria Gomez: quick compare: synthetic-load-run vs replay harness differ: replay has more prefix reuse so KV cache = higher hit rate. Synthetic RPS had lower cache locality yesterday. Could that explain P50?
Jonah Lee: sharing profiling snippet from the failing run (CPU/GPU switch stacks):
```
# perf top excerpt (gpu worker)
+ fused_attn_kernel             43.2%
+ nv_memcpy_async               18.7%
+ kv_cache_lookup               11.1%
+ scheduler_spin                8.9%
+ other                         18.1%
```

Dmitri Chen: that fused_attn % looks high — if kernel selection picks fused-attn for sequences that actually benefit from the matmul path, latency can spike. We changed selection threshold: `if seq_len <= 128 and batch < 4 -> fused_attn` (old: seq_len<=64).
Sam Klein: can you paste the kernel selection rule and commit note? I want an apples-to-apples run.
Dmitri Chen: sure: `runtime/selector.cc` patch snippet:
```
// new heuristic
if (seq_len <= 128 && effective_batch < 4 && !kv_streaming) {
  choose_kernel(FUSED_ATTN);
} else {
  choose_kernel(MATMUL_ATTENTION);
}
```
Commit: 9c3b7f - extend fused-attn threshold for small batches

Elaine Park: note the batching heuristic also changed: `batching/v2` will coalesce up to 12 requests with a 6ms window for throughput mode. For dedicated pools we default to latency-mode but the canary had a config drift to throughput-mode during the deploy.
perf-bot: config-drift-detected: dedicated/us-west-2/pool-42 had `batching.mode` flip from `latency` -> `throughput` at 2026-03-13T02:09:41Z by deploy 9c3b7f
Maria Gomez: that explains KV cache churn: throughput mode forces larger batches and more mixed prefixes -> cache eviction. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 87% -> 62% in affected run. Lower KV hit increases per-token work and worsens p50.
Jonah Lee: reproduce plan I'm running: 1) replay harness with recorded production traces (to match prefix locality) 2) synthetic-sustained RPS with current batch policy 3) apples-to-apples with old selector + old batching. Commands: `./tools/replay --trace=prod-20260312.trace --rate=200 --out=runA` and `./tools/synth --rps=200 --pattern=uniform --out=runB`.
Sam Klein: thanks. Can you also run a focused microbenchmark that isolates kernel perf? e.g., single-request loop that toggles fused vs matmul for seq_len 64/128/256 and measures average kernel time.
Dmitri Chen: done locally, results: fused vs matmul avg lat (ms) for seq_len 64: fused 6.2ms, matmul 5.9ms; seq_len 128: fused 12.4ms, matmul 9.1ms. So fused is worse at 128 for our kernel implementation when memory copies dominate.
Elaine Park: so the heuristic widened the range too far — we should roll back to seq_len<=64 for fused-attn until we optimize the fused kernel memory path.
perf-bot: rollback candidate created: revert 9c3b7f -> PR #2184; auto-smoke recommended.
Sam Klein: before rollback, let's validate if batching-mode flip alone could be the main culprit. Maria, can you run replay with old batch config but current selector and vice versa?
Maria Gomez: running now. run-id A: replay + old-batching + new-selector. run-id B: replay + new-batching + old-selector. I expect A to have smaller regression if batching is the driver.
oncall-bot: alert: dedicated-pool-42 currently at 78% utilization; autoscaler has 4 cold nodes booting (est 45s) — FYI.
Jonah Lee: also measuring scale-up time: observed cold-start tail ~40-55s (vm init + model load). Burst credits were exhausted in this test because we hit a sustained spike. If autoscaler can't refill within 60s, p95 will suffer.
Sam Klein: good catch. Action items: 1) Maria finish the two replay runs and post perf dashboard links; 2) Dmitri revert selector in a canary and microbench fused kernel memory; 3) Elaine revert batching.mode drift in configs; 4) Jonah produce a short-run of cold-start timeline + suggestion for pre-warm policy (keep N warm for burst).
Dmitri Chen: I'll open PR to revert 9c3b7f to canary and add telemetry to log chosen kernel + seq_len + effective_batch to help post-mortem.
Maria Gomez: run results: A (old-batching + new-selector): P50 +3% vs baseline; B (new-batching + old-selector): P50 +12% vs baseline. Link: https://redwood.internal/perf/compare/1759_vs_1760. So batching-mode appears to be the dominant factor here.
Sam Klein: perfect — that points to the config drift as primary. Still keep the selector revert in case fused kernel pathological cases exist.
Elaine Park: rolling config fix to dedicated/us-west-2/pool-42 now. Patch will set `batching.mode=latency` and bump `kv_cache_size=1.5x`.
perf-bot: deploy: config-change-315 applied to pool-42 at 2026-03-16T10:44:12Z by Elaine Park. Auto-run scheduled in 10m.
Sam Klein: thanks everyone. We'll wait for the auto-run. If P50 returns to baseline we close this. If not, follow-up with selector rollback + kernel optimization. :thumbsup:

-- thread end --
